chapter.title: Switching the line on for real

cards.body: For six chapters you have stood at the start of the line and pressed the bell yourself. **The Active toggle hands the bell to the world.** Picture a small switch on the wall beside the belt: you flip it, the lights hum, and you walk out the door. Next morning the bins at the end are full and nobody was there.
cards.simpler: For six chapters you have started the line yourself, every time, by pressing the bell. **The Active toggle hands that bell to the world.** Think of a light switch on the wall next to the belt. You flip it, the machine hums, and you go home. The next morning the bins at the end are full, and nobody had to stand there.

cards.prompt: Priya builds a line: Schedule Trigger at 8am, then post "good morning" to Slack. She clicks Test workflow, sees the message arrive, and goes home. Tomorrow at 8am, what happens?

options.text: Nothing. The line is still off
It posts at 8am, but only to Priya

whyNot.a: That's what the test run did once, not what the schedule does: Test workflow runs the line one time while you watch.
whyNot.c: There's no "only to you" mode: the message goes where the Slack node says, or nowhere at all if the line is off.

cards.reteach: Test workflow is you pressing the bell by hand. The Schedule Trigger only rings on its own once the Active toggle is on. Off means the trigger is asleep, however many times you tested.

cards.title: Test versus Active
cards.body:
There are two ways to start the line. *Test workflow*, the button at the bottom of the editor, runs it once, right now, while you watch. The *Active* toggle at the top right tells n8n something different: listen for the trigger from now on, with or without me.

**Only an active workflow's trigger listens.** A Schedule Trigger does not count the hours while the toggle is off. A form or webhook trigger has two addresses, a test one and a *production* one, and the production one only answers when the workflow is active.

Flip the toggle and n8n asks nothing more. Every run from then on shows up in the Executions list.
cards.simpler: There are two ways to start the line. The Test workflow button runs it once while you watch. The Active toggle tells n8n to keep listening for the trigger after you leave. **Only an active workflow's trigger listens.** A Schedule Trigger does not count the hours while the toggle is off. A form or webhook trigger has a test address and a production address, and the production one only answers when the workflow is active. Every run lands in Executions.

cards.title: Six rows called Dan
cards.body:
Dan runs the front desk at a dental clinic. Every Friday he copied the week's new patient forms into a spreadsheet, about 40 minutes of typing. On Thursday he built the line: Form Trigger, Edit Fields, Google Sheets. He tested it 6 times with his own name and went home pleased.

Friday morning the sheet had 6 rows, every one of them called Dan, and none of the 11 real patients. He had never flipped the toggle. He flipped it at 9:03 and watched the first real row land at 9:41.
cards.simpler: Dan runs a dental clinic's front desk. Every Friday he spent about 40 minutes typing new patient forms into a spreadsheet. On Thursday he built the line: Form Trigger, Edit Fields, Google Sheets. He tested it 6 times with his name and went home. Friday morning the sheet held 6 rows, all called Dan, none of the 11 real patients. **He had never flipped the toggle.** He flipped it at 9:03 and the first real row landed at 9:41.

cards.prompt: Meena's line starts with a form trigger. She wants to send her team the form link. Which link makes the line run once the toggle is on?

options.text: The test URL she used while building
Either one, as long as the toggle is on

whyNot.a: That's the building-time door: the test URL only answers while you have the editor open and press Test workflow.
whyNot.c: The test address is not a second real one: it only listens during a test run, never on its own.

cards.reteach: A form or webhook trigger has two doors. The test door opens only while you are pressing Test workflow. The production door opens only while the Active toggle is on. Share the production one.

cards.title: Before you flip it
cards.body:
Name every node. Open each one and change "Google Sheets" to "Add patient row" and "Slack" to "Tell front desk". Tomorrow a red node called "Add patient row" tells you what jammed. A red node called "Google Sheets1" tells you nothing.

**Pick one real task, and keep it small.** One bell, one job per station, the rule from chapter 1. If your first real line needs more than 6 nodes, cut it in half and switch on the first half.

Know where you will check. Open Executions the next morning. Green rows mean it ran. Red means a jam. No rows at all means the bell never rang, so look at the toggle first.
cards.simpler: Name every node for its job, like "Add patient row" instead of "Google Sheets". A red node with a real name tells you what jammed. "Google Sheets1" tells you nothing. **Pick one real task, and keep it small.** One bell, one job per station. More than 6 nodes? Switch on the first half. Open Executions the next morning. Green rows mean it ran. Red means a jam. No rows means the bell never rang, so check the toggle first.

cards.body: Tomas flips the toggle on, then keeps building for another hour, adding a node, deleting one, saving each change as he goes. Every real run that hour went through whatever half-built line was saved at that moment. Spot it: **if the toggle is on and you are still dragging nodes, flip it off**, finish, test once, then flip it back.
cards.simpler: Tomas flips the toggle on, then keeps building for another hour. He adds a node, deletes one, and saves each change as he goes. Every real run in that hour went through whatever half-built line was saved at that moment. Here is the sign to watch for: **if the toggle is on and you are still dragging nodes, flip it off.** Finish the line, test it once, then flip it back on.

cards.prompt: Next morning, the Executions list for your new line is empty. No green rows, no red ones. What is the most likely cause?

options.text: The toggle was never switched on, so the trigger never rang
Test workflow has to be pressed each morning

whyNot.a: That's a jam, and a jam shows as a red row: an empty list means the line never started at all.
whyNot.c: That's the hand-pressed bell: once active, the trigger rings by itself and Test workflow is not needed.

cards.reteach: A failed run still leaves a mark, a red row. An empty list means no run began, and the usual reason is that the trigger was asleep because the workflow was not active. Check the toggle before you check anything else.

cards.title: In one breath
cards.body: Test workflow runs the line once while you watch. **The Active toggle keeps the trigger listening when you are gone**, so name every station, flip it on, and look at the Executions list tomorrow.
cards.simpler: Test workflow runs the line once while you stand and watch. **The Active toggle keeps the trigger listening when you are gone.** So name every station for its job, flip the toggle on, and open the Executions list tomorrow to see what ran.

cards.body: Tonight: open your chapter 1 workflow, rename each node to what it does, set the schedule for 8am tomorrow, and flip the Active toggle on. At 8:05, open Executions and look for one green row.
cards.simpler: Tonight, open your chapter 1 workflow. Rename each node to say what it does. Set the schedule for 8am tomorrow. Then **flip the Active toggle on** and walk away. At 8:05 tomorrow, open Executions and look for one green row. That row means the line ran without you.

chapter.outcomeLine: You can now switch on one workflow that handles a real task at your job and know exactly where to check that it ran.
